subject: general
question: A dishonest trader claims to sell rice at a profit of 39% but uses a weight of 17% less than the stated value at the time of sale. What is the total percentage profit of the trader? (Round to the nearest whole number)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let 100g of rice cost 100 units.

Selling Price (SP) for 100g stated value = 100 + 39% profit = 139 units.

Actual Cost Price (CP) for weight given (17% less) = 100 − 17 = 83 units.

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100 = [(139 − 83) ÷ 83] × 100.

Profit % = (56 ÷ 83) × 100 ≈ 67.47% ≈ 67%.

**∴ The correct answer is 67%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Claimed profit on sale = 39%

⇒ Less weight used by the trader = 17%

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100
